history.period: Original 16th century per some accounts / mid-18th century per 1880 British report; rebuilt 1921
history.summary: A major Hindu temple near Hathi Gate, Amritsar, dedicated to Goddess Durga. The shrine's sarovar (tank) and 'Devi dwara' are recorded in the Amritsar District Gazetteer of 1893 and in 1868 municipal records, confirming centuries of Hindu pilgrimage to the site. Legend holds that Rama visited this ground during the Ashwamedha Yajna and that Luv and Kush tied Hanuman to the banyan tree here (the tree is still venerated). The present temple was rebuilt in 1921 by Guru Harsai Mal Kapoor deliberately in the architectural style of the Sikh Harmandir Sahib — a gilded dome on a marble causeway in the middle of the sarovar. The foundation stone was laid by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya; sources differ on 1924 vs 1925 (CONFLICT, verify). Its 12x12-ft silver-carved entrance doors give it the name 'Silver Temple'. town_description: Amritsar is a city in northwestern Punjab, founded by the fourth Sikh Guru, Guru Ram Das, in 1577 around the sacred Amrit Sarovar. It is the spiritual and cultural centre of Sikhism, home to the Golden Temple and the Akal Takht. The city is also known for the Jallianwala Bagh memorial, its role in Partition history, and Amritsari cuisine, drawing millions of pilgrims and tourists each year.
